selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 14 or 15, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, as read on Nov. 15. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Two NPR audio segments with no transcript were skipped. Quotes under five words were left out, and two entries that were a commentator's account of what an official said were removed. No original source (transcript, release or post) could be read for any statement, so all wording is as the outlet reported it.
lede: Fifty-six statements by 15 officeholders appeared in two days of NPR and PBS NewsHour politics coverage. Most were about three things: the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop and what it will cost to fix air traffic control, the Iran war and talk of ending it, and what Democrats plan to do with the majorities they won on Nov. 3.

Seven of the 56 were factual claims that data or documents could test. Three were supported, including the transportation secretary's statement that air traffic control has seen decades of underinvestment. Four were unsupported, meaning no evidence was found for them; that is not a finding that they are false. Two of those four are the secretary's reported account of the ground stop investigation, which differs from the FAA's own published account.

The other 49 are opinions, predictions, promises and one personal attack. They are listed because they were said, not because they can be checked. One of them, the Florida governor's statement about what state law requires, turns on how a statute is read; what the statute says is given beside it.

statements.speaker: Ron DeSantis
statements.quote: What they are doing is not mandated by Florida law

source.note: No original transcript or post located.

statements.finding: This turns on how the statute is read. Florida's SB 1134, effective Jan. 1, 2027, bars a municipality from funding or promoting activities designed with reference to ethnicity, among other categories, and exempts content-neutral event permits and recognition of state and federal holidays. It names no parades and requires no cancellation.
statements.context: In a message on X after Delray Beach, Florida, cancelled its St. Patrick's Day parade citing a new state law restricting government-funded diversity initiatives.

statements.finding: FAA capital (Facilities and Equipment) appropriations rose from $2.67 billion in fiscal 2001 to $3.02 billion in fiscal 2021, about 1.6% a year and below inflation, and fell $841 million short of authorized levels under the 2018 authorization, according to the Eno Center for Transportation's tabulation. evidence.label: Eno Center for Transportation, FAA F&E and Operations appropriations 1991-2021

statements.speaker: Sean Duffy
statements.quote: Reported as: He has said the problem began when L3Harris was replacing a section of old copper wire with new fiber wire, somehow causing the system to overload.

source.note: Only the reporter's paraphrase was read; no original statement located.

statements.finding: The FAA's own account differs. It says data from two sites, a radar site in Amarillo, Texas and a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris had deployed a new router, flooded the network; it attributes the instability to the legacy system, not to upgrade work, and says the root cause is still under investigation. L3Harris has not named a cause.

evidence.label: FAA, Nationwide Ground Stop: Questions and Answers (Nov. 15, 2026)

statements.finding: The FAA names two sites, in Amarillo, Texas and El Dorado, Arkansas, and a new router at El Dorado, and says it and L3Harris are still investigating.
